summary: 4x4 matrix multiply with output-alias handling (stdcall, three _BYTE pointers: a1 output, a2 first operand, a3 second operand). When the second operand a3 aliases the output a1 and the first operand does not, a specialized in-place path computes and writes rows directly; when the first operand a2 also aliases the output, a3 is copied to a stack buffer first. The general path multiplies rows of a2 by columns of a3 using x87 dot products and returns a1.

operations.description: Guard on a3 == a1: the second operand aliases the output, entering the alias-handling path.
Guard on a2 != a1: within the alias case, take the specialized in-place path (no stack copy).
Specialized path outer loop over rows (EDI from -4 to 0, 4 iterations), reading column elements of a3 (edx) and advancing the output row v4 by 4 bytes.
Specialized path inner loop (ESI from -16 to 0, 4 iterations) computing one output element per iteration.
x87 accumulation: four fld/fmul products summed on the stack and stored as a float into the output row (v4[4*ESI+64] = _ET1).
qmemcpy copies 64 bytes of a3 into the stack buffer v16 when a2 also aliases the output (a2 == a1).
a3 = v16: the general path reads the second operand from the stack copy instead of the live output.
General path outer loop over rows (v13 from -4 to 0, 4 iterations), advancing the operand row pointer ECX and output pointer v10 by 16 bytes each.
General path inner loop (ESI from -4 to 0, 4 iterations) computing one output element per iteration.
x87 dot-product accumulation: products of the a2 row (ecx) with a3 column elements (edx+esi*4+10h..40h) are summed and stored as a float (v10[4*ESI+16] = _ET1).
